Chapter 9 — Communications, Means of Transport and Development of Human Resources (Communication, Transportation and Human Resources Development)

In means of transport (coming and going) (Transportation) these are included: railways, roads, sea ships and aircraft; whereas in means of communications (news-giving) (Communication) these are included: post, wire (telegram), telephone, mobile phone, telex, fax, radio, television and computer etc. All these means play an important role in the economic, social and political progress of any country. Their existence is very necessary for strengthening defence, making administration stable, maintaining peace and order, and promoting culture, civilisation, knowledge and skill. National integrity and prosperity are linked with them. Here we state their economic, social and political benefits (especially with reference to Pakistan).

Importance and usefulness of means of communications and transport (Importance)

Economic benefits

In economic terms means of coming and going have the following benefits:

1. Taking raw material to factories

With the help of means of transport raw material is lifted from the places where it is produced and taken to factories, e.g. with the help of bullock carts, trucks and railways cotton is lifted from fields and taken to cloth mills. If facilities for bringing raw material to factories did not exist, then on one side factories would remain closed and on the other side these things would lie and rot in the fields.

2. Taking manufactures to markets

Things made in factories are taken to different cities and markets, so that the needy can buy them; e.g. shoes prepared in the Bata factory are taken to show-rooms throughout the country.

3. End of self-sufficient life

By virtue of transport the trend of self-sufficient life (i.e. fulfilling one’s needs oneself) of our villages and backward areas has ended, and a link is being established between them and cities. In old times it used to be said that our villages depend on cities only for salt, matches and kerosene oil, because they prepared the remaining things of need themselves. But today, because of the progress of means of transport, such a deep link has arisen between cities and villages that villagers too have begun using refrigerators, televisions, tractors, mobiles and scores of such things which are prepared in overseas countries.

Chapter 9 — Communications, Means of Transport and Development of Human Resources (Communication, Transportation and Human Resources Development)

In means of transport (coming and going) (Transportation) these are included: railways, roads, sea ships and aircraft; whereas in means of communications (news-giving) (Communication) these are included: post, wire (telegram), telephone, mobile phone, telex, fax, radio, television and computer etc. All these means play an important role in the economic, social and political progress of any country. Their existence is very necessary for strengthening defence, making administration stable, maintaining peace and order, and promoting culture, civilisation, knowledge and skill. National integrity and prosperity are linked with them. Here we state their economic, social and political benefits (especially with reference to Pakistan).

Importance and usefulness of means of communications and transport (Importance)

Economic benefits

In economic terms means of coming and going have the following benefits:

1. Taking raw material to factories

With the help of means of transport raw material is lifted from the places where it is produced and taken to factories, e.g. with the help of bullock carts, trucks and railways cotton is lifted from fields and taken to cloth mills. If facilities for bringing raw material to factories did not exist, then on one side factories would remain closed and on the other side these things would lie and rot in the fields.

2. Taking manufactures to markets

Things made in factories are taken to different cities and markets, so that the needy can buy them; e.g. shoes prepared in the Bata factory are taken to show-rooms throughout the country.

3. End of self-sufficient life

By virtue of transport the trend of self-sufficient life (i.e. fulfilling one’s needs oneself) of our villages and backward areas has ended, and a link is being established between them and cities. In old times it used to be said that our villages depend on cities only for salt, matches and kerosene oil, because they prepared the remaining things of need themselves. But today, because of the progress of means of transport, such a deep link has arisen between cities and villages that villagers too have begun using refrigerators, televisions, tractors, mobiles and scores of such things which are prepared in overseas countries.

4. Expansion in division of labour (Division of Labour)

By virtue of transport the circle of division of labour (i.e. dividing work among themselves) also becomes wide, because the different areas of the country obtain specialisation in producing only those things which they can prepare at low cost, and later exchange them with the things of one another. In this way every area becomes able to use the things produced in other areas; as the different areas of Pakistan obtain sports goods from Sialkot, electric fans from Gujrat, walnuts from Parachinar and dates from Sukkur.

By virtue of means of transport, goods produced in different factories and areas reach every corner of the country. Among shopkeepers there is complete competition and in this way their prices become the same everywhere; you buy a tin of Dalda ghee from Lahore or from Peshawar, it will be obtained at the same price.

sections.content:
4. Expansion in division of labour (Division of Labour)

By virtue of transport the circle of division of labour (i.e. dividing work among themselves) also becomes wide, because the different areas of the country obtain specialisation in producing only those things which they can prepare at low cost, and later exchange them with the things of one another. In this way every area becomes able to use the things produced in other areas; as the different areas of Pakistan obtain sports goods from Sialkot, electric fans from Gujrat, walnuts from Parachinar and dates from Sukkur.

5. Uniformity in prices

By virtue of means of transport, goods produced in different factories and areas reach every corner of the country. Among shopkeepers there is complete competition and in this way their prices become the same everywhere; you buy a tin of Dalda ghee from Lahore or from Peshawar, it will be obtained at the same price.

6. Mobility of labourers (Mobility of Labour)

With the help of means of transport labourers can easily reach from one place to another place. An increase occurs in their mobility; the rate of wages becomes the same, and all factories get labourers according to their need.

7. Benefiting from natural resources

If resources of coming and going did not exist, benefit could not be taken from many such natural resources as are situated in remote places and to which access could not be possible.

8. Suitable distribution of necessities

By virtue of means of transport, the thing that is prepared in some areas in excess of local need can be taken from there to those areas where it is scarce. As it were, every thing is distributed automatically in the different areas of the country according to their need.

9. Increase in employment opportunities

Many people get employment. In Pakistan, in the Railway department, road transport, PIA and other airlines, lakhs of individuals are doing jobs. At this time six per cent of employed individuals are engaged in this sector.

10. Regional spread of population

By virtue of means of transport the country’s population does not become dense at a few places, but spreads in different areas of the country, and thus backward areas too progress. Because of good communications an increase occurs in foreign tourists, investment and government income.

Social benefits (Social Benefits)

From the social point of view too means of coming and going have many benefits. People get the opportunity to meet one another and exchange ideas; they learn a lot from one another. Civilisation and culture flourish; educational spread occurs. Today the poetry of Allama Iqbal of the land of Punjab creates the same spirit and zeal in all Pakistanis as does that of Khushhal Khan Khattak of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and of Shah Latif Bhitai of Sindh.
